entries.english_requirement: Cover 8-to-1 multiplexer behavior for every select value, toggling of each data input bit, and the output value observed for each select.
Cover 3-to-8 decoder behavior for all select values with the enable asserted, the all-zero output when enable is deasserted, and the cross of select against enable.
Cover 8-to-3 encoder behavior for each one-hot input, the encoded output value for each, and the valid flag in both asserted and deasserted states.
Cover 4-bit adder behavior across the full input range for both operands, both carry-in states, and the carry-out asserted and deasserted, crossing carry-in against carry-out.
Cover 32-bit adder behavior across low, mid, and high value ranges for both operands and the sum, including zero and maximum boundaries, and the overflow carry-out in both states.
Cover 8-bit subtractor behavior for operand ranges, the zero and maximum difference values, and the borrow output asserted when the subtrahend exceeds the minuend.
Cover 8-bit comparator behavior for the greater-than, equal, and less-than outputs, ensuring each is asserted at least once and that exactly one is active per comparison.
Cover 8-bit ALU behavior for every opcode, operand value ranges, the zero flag in both states, and the cross of opcode against the zero flag to confirm each operation can produce zero.
Cover 8-bit barrel shifter behavior for every shift amount including zero and maximum, both shift directions, and the cross of direction against shift amount.
Cover 8-bit parity generator behavior for both even and odd parity results, the all-zero and all-one inputs, and inputs across a spread of set-bit counts.
Cover the 3-input majority voter for all eight input combinations and both output values, confirming the output follows the majority of the inputs.
Cover 4-bit binary-to-Gray conversion across the full input range including the zero and maximum values, and confirm every Gray output code is produced.
Cover 4-bit Gray-to-binary conversion for every Gray input code and confirm the full range of binary outputs is produced.
Cover BCD adder behavior for all valid decimal digit operands, both carry-in states, the carry-out generated when the result exceeds nine, and treat non-decimal operand values as illegal.
Cover the seven-segment decoder for all ten decimal digit inputs, the blanked output for invalid inputs, and confirm each distinct segment pattern is produced.
Cover the 8-bit population counter for every possible set-bit count from zero through eight, including the all-zero and all-one inputs.
Cover the one-hot detector for genuine one-hot inputs, the all-zero input, and multi-bit inputs, crossing the input class against the detector output.
Cover the 8-bit absolute value unit for positive, negative, and zero inputs, including the most-negative input where the magnitude cannot be represented.
Cover the min/max selector for cases where the first operand is larger, the second is larger, and the two are equal, across low and high operand ranges.
Cover the sign extension unit for positive and negative inputs, the zero input, and the extreme representable values, confirming the upper bits replicate the sign.
Cover the enabled 2-to-1 multiplexer for both select values and all data input combinations while enabled, and the forced-zero output while disabled.
Cover the 2x2 crossbar for both the pass-through and swapped configurations across all input combinations, crossing the swap control against the input pattern.
Cover the 4-input lookup table for every address value, and the output in both states, crossing address against output to confirm each table entry is exercised.
Cover the tri-state buffer with the output enable asserted for a spread of data values and deasserted for the high-impedance state, crossing enable against data.
Cover the D flip-flop capturing both data values on the clock edge, the asynchronous reset forcing the output low, and the transition of the output in both directions.
Cover the enabled D flip-flop loading new data when the enable is asserted, holding its value when the enable is deasserted, and the cross of enable against data.
Cover the T flip-flop toggling its output when the toggle input is asserted, holding when deasserted, and both output transition directions.
Cover the JK flip-flop across all four input combinations covering hold, reset, set, and toggle behaviour, and both output transition directions.
Cover the 8-bit register loading data across value ranges, holding its contents when load is deasserted, the reset-to-zero behaviour, and the cross of load against data range.
Cover the left shift register serially loading both bit values, the all-zero and all-one register states, and the serial output bit shifting out in both states.
Cover the bidirectional shift register shifting in both directions, holding when disabled, and the cross of direction against enable to confirm every mode is exercised.

Cover the 8-bit up counter reaching its maximum value and wrapping around to zero on the next enabled clock edge, holding its value while the enable is deasserted, and the reset returning the count to zero.
Cover the 4-bit down counter decrementing to zero, underflowing from zero back to the maximum value, the zero flag asserting, and holding while disabled.
Cover the up/down counter counting in both directions, wrapping at the maximum when counting up and underflowing at zero when counting down, and the cross of direction against enable.
Cover the modulo-N counter reaching its terminal count, rolling over to zero, asserting the terminal count flag, and holding while the enable is deasserted.
Cover the ring counter visiting every one-hot state, completing a full rotation back to the initial state, and treating any non-one-hot state as illegal.
Cover the Johnson counter visiting all eight valid states in its sequence, completing a full cycle, and holding while the enable is deasserted.
Cover the Gray counter producing every Gray code value, wrapping from the last code back to zero, and holding while disabled, confirming only one bit changes per step.
Cover the BCD decade counter visiting every decimal digit, rolling over from nine to zero, asserting the carry output on rollover, and never entering a non-decimal state.
Cover the 8-bit linear feedback shift register producing values across its range, the seed value after reset, the feedback bit in both states, and the all-zero lock-up state treated as illegal.
Cover the accumulator summing input values across ranges, holding when disabled, clearing on reset, and asserting the overflow flag when the accumulated total wraps.
Cover the edge detector asserting the rising-edge pulse on a low-to-high input transition and the falling-edge pulse on a high-to-low transition, with neither asserted while the input is steady.
Cover the debouncer holding its output stable while the input is bouncing, propagating a change only after the input has been stable for the full count, and both output states.
Cover the pulse generator emitting exactly one cycle of output pulse per trigger assertion, remaining low while the trigger is held, and rearming after the trigger is released.
Cover the clock divider producing both output phases, the internal divide counter across its full range, and the output toggling only while the enable is asserted.
Cover the two-stage synchronizer propagating both input values through to the output, and both output transition directions after the synchronization delay.

Cover the synchronous FIFO going both full and empty, simultaneous read and write while partially filled, write attempts while full and read attempts while empty being rejected, and the cross of write against read enables.
Cover the stack pushing until full, popping until empty, push attempts while full and pop attempts while empty being ignored, and the cross of push against pop.
Cover the single-port RAM writing and reading across the low, middle, and high address ranges, the boundary addresses, and the cross of write enable against address range.
Cover the dual-port RAM writing on port A while reading on port B, both ports addressing the same location simultaneously, and address coverage across the full range on both ports.
Cover the ROM being read at every address including the first and last entries, and confirm the returned data spans the zero, mid-range, and maximum stored values.

Cover the register file writing to every register, reading from both read ports across the full address range, the read-during-write hazard where a read address matches the write address, and register zero being addressed.
Cover the CAM reporting a match when the searched value is present and no match when absent, matches at the first and last entries, and writes to every entry.
Cover the circular buffer wrapping its write and read pointers past the end of storage, the occupancy count spanning empty through full, and simultaneous read and write.
Cover the shift-register FIFO filling from empty to full, the valid flag asserting once data is present, and data propagating through every stage.
Cover the byte-enabled scratchpad writing with each byte-enable pattern including none and all bytes enabled, across the address range, crossing byte enable against write enable.
Cover the FIFO watermark flags asserting and deasserting as occupancy crosses the programmable thresholds, and the occupancy transitioning across each watermark boundary in both directions.
Cover the mailbox accepting a message when empty, rejecting a put while occupied, delivering on get, and the occupied flag transitioning in both directions.
Cover the traffic light FSM visiting every state, each legal state transition in sequence, the full cycle returning to the initial state, and holding in a state while the timer has not expired.
Cover the vending machine accumulating each accepted coin value, reaching and exceeding the item price, dispensing the item, and returning change when overpaid.
Cover the Moore sequence detector visiting every state, detecting the target pattern, the overlapping detection case, and returning to the idle state on a mismatching bit.
Cover the Mealy sequence detector across all states, the detection output asserting combinationally on the final input bit, and each state transition taken for both input values.
Cover the fixed priority arbiter granting each requester, the no-request idle case, simultaneous requests resolving to the highest priority, and confirm the grant is always one-hot or zero.
Cover the round-robin arbiter granting every requester in turn, rotating priority after each grant, handling simultaneous requests fairly, and the idle case with no requests.
Cover the valid-ready handshake for all four combinations of valid and ready, the transfer occurring only when both are asserted, valid waiting for ready, and back-to-back transfers.
Cover the APB slave through its idle, setup, and access phases, both read and write transfers, the ready signal inserting wait states, and the address range covered on both transfer types.
Cover the UART transmitter through idle, start bit, all data bit positions, and stop bit states, transmitting both all-zero and all-one data payloads, and the busy flag across a full frame.
Cover the UART receiver detecting the start bit, sampling every data bit position, validating the stop bit, asserting the received-data valid flag, and flagging a framing error on a bad stop bit.
Cover the SPI master asserting and releasing chip select, shifting all eight bit positions, both clock phases within a transfer, and the busy flag spanning a complete transaction.
Cover the I2C condition detector recognising a start condition when data falls while clock is high, a stop condition when data rises while clock is high, and neither during normal data transitions.
Cover the 4-bit array multiplier for zero, unity, and maximum operands, the full product range including the maximum product, and the cross of the two operand ranges.
Cover the sequential multiplier through every iteration of its shift-add loop, the start and done handshake, zero and maximum operands, and the multiplier bit determining whether an add occurs.
Cover the sequential divider producing quotients across the value range, a zero remainder for exact division, the divide-by-zero error flag, and the done handshake completing each operation.
Cover the multiply-accumulate unit accumulating products across operand ranges, the clear operation resetting the accumulator, holding when disabled, and the overflow flag asserting.
Cover the CRC-8 generator processing both input bit values, the CRC register spanning its value range, the initial value after reset, and the feedback path being exercised in both states.
Cover the FIR filter tap for zero, positive, and maximum sample and coefficient values, the delay line propagating samples, and the accumulated output range.
Cover the watchdog timer counting up towards its limit, being kicked before expiry to reload the counter, expiring and asserting the timeout, and the counter spanning its range.
Cover the PWM generator at zero, partial, and full duty-cycle settings, the output asserted and deasserted within a period, the counter wrapping at the end of each period, and holding while disabled.
Cover the interrupt controller with each interrupt source asserted, masked and unmasked, multiple simultaneous interrupts, and the aggregated output asserting only when an unmasked source is pending.
Cover the compare timer counting to the compare value, asserting the match output, restarting from zero after a match, compare values at the extremes, and holding while disabled.
Cover the clock gate enabling and disabling the gated output, the enable being latched on the correct clock phase, and both transition directions of the latched enable.
Cover 2-to-1 multiplexer behavior for all combinations of select and input values.
Cover 4-to-1 multiplexer behavior for all select values, input bit toggling, and output value per select combination.
Cover full adder behavior for all combinations of inputs a, b, cin and resulting sum, cout outputs.
Cover 8-bit adder behavior across low, mid, and high value ranges for inputs a, b and resulting sum, including boundary and overflow conditions.
Cover 4-bit priority encoder behavior for all priority levels of input d and corresponding encoded output y, including cross coverage of legal input-output combinations.
Cover 2-to-4 decoder behavior for all select values and the corresponding one-hot output, treating non-one-hot outputs as illegal.
Cover 16-to-1 multiplexer behavior for every select value, both output values, and the cross of select against the observed output.
Cover the 1-to-4 demultiplexer routing the input to each output port, the all-zero output when the enable is deasserted, and the cross of select against enable and input data.

Cover the 8-bit priority encoder resolving each single request line, the no-request case with valid deasserted, simultaneous requests where the lowest index wins, and the cross of the encoded index against the valid flag.

Cover the 4-bit carry-lookahead adder for the carry-in both clear and set, full carry propagation across all four bit positions, carry generation from the low bits, and the carry-out asserted and deasserted.
Cover the 16-bit carry-select adder with the internal block carry both taken and not taken, operands at their zero and maximum values, and the final carry-out asserted.
Cover the 8-bit incrementer at the zero and maximum input values, the wrap producing an overflow flag, and the pass-through behavior when the enable is deasserted.
Cover the 8-bit decrementer at zero where it underflows and asserts borrow, at the maximum value, and the hold case when the enable is deasserted.
Cover the 4-bit equality comparator matching on the all-zero and all-one operands, mismatching in each single bit position, and both states of the equal and not-equal outputs.
Cover the 4-bit logic unit executing every opcode, operands at their zero and all-one extremes, and the cross of opcode against each operand pattern.
Cover the 8-bit arithmetic right shifter for every shift amount, sign extension of negative operands, the zero-shift pass-through, and the cross of shift amount against operand sign.
Cover the 8-bit rotator for both rotate directions, every rotate amount including zero, and the cross of direction against amount.
Cover the 8-bit parity checker under both even and odd parity modes, data words with even and odd numbers of set bits, and the error flag both asserted and clear.
Cover the 8-bit bit-reversal unit on palindromic patterns that map to themselves, on walking-one patterns that map to the opposite end, and on the all-zero and all-one words.

Cover the count-leading-zeros unit for every possible leading-zero count, the all-zero input that yields the maximum count with the zero flag set, and the case where the most significant bit is already set.
Cover the count-trailing-zeros unit for every trailing-zero count, the all-zero input that saturates the count, and inputs where only the least or most significant bit is set.
Cover the byte-wide 4-to-1 multiplexer selecting each of the four input words, the all-zero and all-one payloads on the selected word, and the cross of select against the output value class.
Cover the binary-to-BCD converter across single-digit, two-digit and three-digit input ranges, the zero and maximum inputs, every hundreds digit value, and digit values at their nine boundary.
Cover the BCD-to-binary converter for every legal digit value on both digits, the zero and ninety-nine extremes, and rejection of illegal digit encodings above nine.
Cover the BCD to excess-3 code converter for every legal BCD digit, the zero and nine boundary digits, the resulting excess-3 codes, and the invalid flag raised on non-BCD inputs.
Cover the Hamming (7,4) encoder for the all-zero and all-one data words, each single data bit set on its own, and both values of every generated parity bit.
Cover the Hamming (7,4) decoder with a zero syndrome for clean codewords, every non-zero syndrome value corresponding to a single-bit error position, and the correction flag both asserted and clear.
Cover the unsigned saturating adder producing a normal in-range sum, a sum that lands exactly on the maximum, and a sum that overflows and clamps with the saturate flag asserted.
Cover the unsigned saturating subtractor for a normal positive difference, an exact-zero difference, and an underflow that clamps to zero with the saturate flag asserted.
Cover the range limiter passing values that fall inside the window, clamping at the lower and upper bounds, the degenerate case where the bounds are equal, and both clamp flags.
Cover the radix-4 Booth encoder producing every recode value from negative two through positive two, each three-bit input window, and the cross of the recode magnitude against the negate flag.
entries.rtl:
module booth_enc3(win, neg, zero, two_x);
  input [2:0] win;
  output reg neg, zero, two_x;
  always @(*) begin
    case (win)
      3'b000: begin neg=1'b0; zero=1'b1; two_x=1'b0; end
      3'b001: begin neg=1'b0; zero=1'b0; two_x=1'b0; end
      3'b010: begin neg=1'b0; zero=1'b0; two_x=1'b0; end
      3'b011: begin neg=1'b0; zero=1'b0; two_x=1'b1; end
      3'b100: begin neg=1'b1; zero=1'b0; two_x=1'b1; end
      3'b101: begin neg=1'b1; zero=1'b0; two_x=1'b0; end
      3'b110: begin neg=1'b1; zero=1'b0; two_x=1'b0; end
      3'b111: begin neg=1'b0; zero=1'b1; two_x=1'b0; end
    endcase
  end
endmodule

entries.english_requirement: Cover the 16-bit zero detector on the all-zero word, on words with only a single bit set in either half, and on the all-one word, crossing the per-half zero flags.

Cover the 32-bit endianness swapper in both pass-through and swapped modes, on the all-zero and all-one words, on words where a single byte lane is non-zero, and the cross of mode against byte pattern.
Cover the mask generator for every mask length from zero through eight, the empty and full mask outputs, and the cross of length against the resulting mask class.
Cover the thermometer-to-binary converter for every legal thermometer code including the empty and full codes, and for illegal non-monotonic codes that raise the error flag.
Cover the one-hot selected multiplexer driving from each of the four sources, the idle case with no select bit set, and the error flag raised when more than one select bit is asserted.
Cover the SR flip-flop being set, being reset, holding its value when both inputs are low, the illegal case with both inputs high, and the transitions between the set and reset states.
Cover the level-sensitive D latch passing data while the enable is high, holding the last value while the enable is low, and every combination of data value against enable level.
Cover the 16-bit LFSR shifting through non-zero states, the feedback tap producing both values, the seed load overriding the shift, and the lockup state being flagged.

Cover the loadable 8-bit counter loading an external value, counting up from the loaded value, wrapping from the maximum back to zero, holding while disabled, and the priority of load over count enable.

Cover the two-digit BCD counter rolling the ones digit from nine to zero, carrying into the tens digit, rolling the full count from ninety-nine back to zero, and never producing an illegal digit above nine.

Cover the programmable prescaler for the minimum and maximum divide ratios, the tick pulse asserted for exactly one cycle, the divider reloading after each tick, and a ratio change taking effect on the following period.

Cover the three-stage pipeline register filling from empty, draining back to empty, holding data under a stall, the valid bit propagating through every stage, and the cross of stall against stage occupancy.
Cover the four-tap programmable delay line at every selectable tap position, data propagating from the input through to the deepest tap, and the cross of tap select against the delayed output value.
Cover the dual-edge detector flagging rising edges, falling edges, both edges through the combined output, and steady high and low levels with no edge reported.

Cover the glitch filter rejecting pulses shorter than the stability window, accepting an input that stays stable for the full window, the stability counter reaching its threshold, and the filtered output changing in both directions.
Cover the parallel-in serial-out shift register loading a full word, shifting out every bit position, the busy flag spanning a complete transfer, and both all-zero and all-one payloads.

Cover the serial-in parallel-out shift register accumulating every bit position, the done flag pulsing when a full word has arrived, the assembled word taking its all-zero and all-one values, and the counter wrapping for the next word.
Cover the universal shift register in all four modes covering hold, shift right, shift left and parallel load, the serial inputs at both values, and the cross of mode against the register contents.

Cover the asynchronous-assert synchronous-release reset synchronizer through the assertion, both stages of the release pipeline, the fully released state, and re-assertion while the pipeline is still filling.

Cover the pulse synchronizer toggling its request on every source pulse, the destination toggle chain settling, the output pulse generated once per source pulse, and back-to-back pulses arriving before the previous one has crossed.

Cover the Gray-coded pointer synchronizer where only one bit changes per update, the synchronized value tracking the source after two clocks, and the full Gray sequence being observed on both source and destination sides.
Cover the token bucket refilling to its maximum, draining to empty, granting a request only when a token is available, denying requests when empty, and simultaneous refill and consume.
Cover the stopwatch running, pausing and resetting, seconds rolling over into minutes, the minute field reaching its maximum, and the cross of the run control against the reset control.

Cover the frequency counter accumulating input edges over a gate window, latching the result when the window closes, resetting the accumulator for the next window, and saturating when the count exceeds the register width.
Cover the duty-cycle measurement block counting high time and total period, latching both values at the end of a period, and measuring the always-low, always-high and balanced duty cases.
Cover the sample-and-hold register capturing on the sample strobe, holding across many idle cycles, capturing the minimum and maximum input values, and back-to-back sample strobes.
Cover the saturating counter incrementing to its maximum and sticking there, decrementing to zero and sticking there, and the cross of the increment and decrement controls at both saturation limits.

Cover the retriggerable one-shot firing on a trigger, holding its output for the full programmed width, being retriggered before expiry to extend the pulse, and returning to idle after the timer expires.

Cover the running set-bit counter accumulating over a serial stream, the count reaching zero and its maximum, the clear control resetting the accumulator, and the cross of the input bit against the clear control.

Cover the running checksum accumulator summing bytes, wrapping past the register maximum with the carry folded back, clearing on command, and the cross of the accumulated value against the carry-out flag.

Cover the programmable terminal-count counter wrapping at the smallest and largest terminal values, the terminal-count flag pulsing exactly at the limit, a terminal value change mid-count, and the counter exceeding a newly lowered limit.

Cover the register pair supporting independent loads and an atomic swap, both registers holding their zero and maximum values, the swap taking priority over a load, and repeated swaps returning the original arrangement.
Cover the bitwise toggle register flipping each bit position independently, toggling every bit at once, holding when the mask is empty, and the register reaching its all-zero and all-one values.

Cover the asynchronous FIFO reaching full and empty across clock domains, the Gray-coded pointers changing one bit at a time, writes blocked while full and reads blocked while empty, and both pointers wrapping through zero.

Cover the skid buffer passing data straight through when the downstream is ready, capturing into the skid slot when back-pressure appears, draining the skid slot afterwards, and never dropping a beat while the slot is occupied.

Cover the single-port RAM arbitrating a simultaneous read and write to the same address, reads and writes to different addresses, the write-priority behavior, and accesses at the first and last address.

design_context.type: single-port RAM with read/write conflict handling

entries.english_requirement: Cover the true dual-port RAM with independent reads and writes on both ports, a write collision when both ports target the same address, port A and port B each accessing the first and last address, and both ports idle.
Cover the direct-mapped cache producing hits and misses, every cache set index being accessed, the valid bit transitioning from clear to set on a fill, and tag matches and mismatches on a valid line.
Cover the cache line state bits moving through invalid, clean and dirty, a write marking a clean line dirty, a writeback returning a dirty line to clean, and invalidation from every state.
Cover the tag array writing and comparing tags at every way, matching and mismatching tags, the valid bits filling from empty to fully populated, and a lookup against an entirely invalid array.

Cover the two-way LRU replacement policy tracking the least recently used way after accesses to either way, the victim selection flipping after each access, and repeated accesses to the same way leaving the victim unchanged.
Cover the guarded stack pushing to full and popping to empty, overflow and underflow errors being flagged and the pointer being held, simultaneous push and pop, and the pointer visiting every depth.

Cover the four-entry priority queue inserting entries at every priority level, dequeuing the highest priority entry first, the queue reaching full and empty, and insertion of a new highest priority ahead of existing entries.

Cover the dual-port RAM forwarding path in both read-first and write-first modes, a same-address read during a write with the bypass engaged, different-address accesses with the bypass idle, and the mode changing between accesses.

Cover the sine lookup ROM across every quadrant of the phase input, the phase values at zero, the quarter, half and three-quarter points, and the output taking its minimum, midpoint and maximum values.
Cover the RAM-based delay line for the shortest and longest programmable delays, the write and read pointers wrapping around the buffer, and data emerging exactly after the configured delay.

Cover the ping-pong buffer swapping between the two banks, writes going to the active bank while reads drain the other, the swap request being honored only when the write bank is complete, and both banks being selected as the write target.

Cover the multi-bank memory selecting each bank, accesses at the first and last offset within a bank, bank switching between consecutive accesses, and the cross of bank select against the write enable.

Cover the parity-protected memory storing and reading back clean data, a single-bit error being detected on read, error injection at each byte lane, and the error flag being cleared by a subsequent clean read.

Cover the two-requester memory arbiter granting each port, resolving simultaneous requests by alternating the winner, the idle case with no requests, and a requester waiting while the other is served.

Cover the memory-mapped register bank writing and reading every register offset, read-only registers rejecting writes, an access to an unmapped offset raising an error, and the cross of the offset against the write enable.
Cover the hash bucket table inserting into every bucket, a bucket collision when a second key hashes to an occupied slot, lookups that hit and miss, and the occupancy vector filling completely.
Cover the descriptor ring producing and consuming entries, the head pointer wrapping around the ring, the ring reaching full and empty, and the ownership bit flipping between producer and consumer.

Cover the overlapping 1101 sequence detector visiting every state, detecting back-to-back overlapping matches, restarting the partial match on a mismatch, and the detect output asserting for exactly one cycle per match.
Cover the elevator controller visiting every floor and every state, moving up and down, opening and closing the doors at each floor, and requests arriving while the car is already moving.

Cover the electronic door lock FSM accepting a correct code digit by digit, rejecting on any wrong digit, the lockout state after repeated failures, the attempt counter reaching its limit, and the unlock output asserting only in the unlocked state.

Cover the ATM controller FSM through card insertion, PIN verification, transaction selection, dispensing and ejection, a PIN failure returning to the card state, and an insufficient balance rejecting the withdrawal.

Cover the washing machine controller running the full cycle through fill, wash, rinse, spin and done, the door interlock pausing the cycle, the timer expiring in each phase, and a cancel returning the machine to idle.

Cover the weighted arbiter granting each requester, the weight counter of the served port decrementing to zero, the weights reloading when all are exhausted, and a high-weight port winning repeatedly against a low-weight port.

Cover the two-level arbiter selecting between the high and low priority groups, granting each requester inside a group, the low group being starved while high requests persist, and the idle case with no requests.

Cover the four-phase request-acknowledge handshake through all four phases in order, the requester waiting for the acknowledge to drop before starting again, and both signals idle between transactions.

Cover the credit-based flow control issuing credits, consuming them on each transmitted beat, blocking transmission when the credit count reaches zero, the counter saturating at its maximum, and simultaneous credit return and consumption.

Cover the AXI-Stream interface with every combination of valid and ready, back-pressure stalling a valid beat, the last beat terminating a packet, single-beat and multi-beat packets, and the beat counter spanning a burst.
Cover the AXI-Lite write channel completing address and data handshakes in either order, the write response phase, every response code, and the channel returning to idle between transactions.

Cover the AHB slave FSM handling idle, non-sequential and sequential transfers, inserting wait states with the ready signal low, both read and write directions, every transfer size, and the error response.

Cover the Wishbone slave completing read and write cycles, the strobe and cycle signals qualifying an access, the acknowledge terminating the cycle, the error termination, and idle cycles between transfers.

Cover the I2C master FSM issuing a start condition, shifting out all address and data bits, sampling the acknowledge bit as both acknowledge and not-acknowledge, issuing a stop condition, and both read and write directions.

Cover the SPI slave shifting in and out all eight bit positions, chip select being asserted and deasserted, a transfer aborted mid-word by chip select going inactive, and both idle and active shift states.

Cover the UART baud rate generator at the smallest and largest divisor settings, the tick and half-tick strobes firing, the divisor counter wrapping every period, and a divisor change taking effect on the next period.

Cover the UART parity checker in all three parity modes covering none, even and odd, data words with even and odd weight, the framing stop bit being correct and corrupted, and the combined error output.
Cover the Manchester encoder producing both half-bit phases for a zero and for a one, the phase toggling every half bit period, and the encoded output changing in both directions.

Cover the Manchester decoder recovering zero and one bits from both half-bit samples, detecting a coding violation when both halves match, the synchronized and unsynchronized states, and the valid output pulsing once per recovered bit.

Cover the running disparity tracker with both disparity polarities, balanced symbols leaving the disparity unchanged, unbalanced symbols flipping it, and the disparity error flag raised on an illegal symbol weight.

Cover the CRC-16 generator processing zero and one input bits, the feedback term taking both values, the register being initialized and holding, and the accumulated remainder reaching its all-zero and all-one values.

Cover the one's complement checksum accumulating words, the end-around carry being folded back, the accumulator reaching zero and its maximum, clearing before a new message, and the final complemented result.

Cover the additive scrambler with its shift register spanning non-zero states, both feedback values, the seed being loaded, the bypass mode passing data unchanged, and the scrambled output taking both values.

Cover the non-restoring divider through every iteration step, the partial remainder going negative and being corrected, division by zero raising the error flag, quotients at zero and the maximum, and the done flag ending the operation.

Cover the Booth multiplier through every iteration, each recode action covering add, subtract and skip, signed operands of both polarities, the zero-operand shortcut, and the product reaching its extreme values.

Cover the three-stage pipelined multiplier with valid flowing through every stage, back-to-back issue keeping all stages busy, a bubble emptying the pipeline, and operands at their zero and maximum values.

Cover the CORDIC rotation engine through every iteration index, the rotation direction taking both signs, the angle accumulator converging toward zero, and the busy and done flags across a full rotation.

Cover the fixed-point rounding unit in truncate, round-to-nearest and round-half-to-even modes, guard bits at the exact halfway point and above and below it, both signs of the input, and the saturation flag on overflow.

shift_en asserted at the same time, confirming load takes priority. Cover both
of them deasserted so the register holds. Cover shifting in a one and shifting
in a zero. Cover the register holding all zeros and all ones. Cover a bit being
shifted all the way from the input to serial_out, which takes eight shifts.
Cover reset asserted while a shift is in progress.

entries.english_requirement:
Cover the FIFO becoming completely full and completely empty, and every
occupancy level in between. Cover a simultaneous read and write while the FIFO
is partially filled, so the occupancy stays unchanged. Cover a write attempted
while the FIFO is full and a read attempted while it is empty, confirming both
are rejected without corrupting the occupancy. Cover the cross of the write
enable against the read enable, and the cross of each enable against the full
and empty flags. Cover the data input at its minimum, maximum and mid-range
values, and cover the reset asserted while the FIFO holds data.

deasserted, including holding at 0 and holding at 15. Cover an asynchronous
reset asserted both while the counter is counting and while it is held.

entries.english_requirement:
Cover every state of the traffic light controller: red, green and yellow. Cover
every legal transition between them: red to green, green to yellow, and yellow
back to red. Cover the red state being held because the sensor is inactive even
though the timer has expired, and cover it being held because the timer has not
yet expired. Cover the sensor asserted and deasserted in each state. Confirm the
three output lights are mutually exclusive: exactly one is on at any time.
